_meta.purpose: A real, cited calisthenics + Pilates progression synthesis for the Fit & Fed workout module, replacing the [Skill Node]/TBD placeholders sitemap.md deliberately left in place pending this research.
_meta.confidenceStatement: This is a well-sourced SYNTHESIS of multiple independently published, publicly documented calisthenics coaching systems and the classical Pilates mat curriculum. It is NOT a clinically validated program: no qualified strength coach, physiotherapist, or certified Pilates instructor reviewed or signed off on this specific tree, its exact ordering, or its exact thresholds. research/product-research.md Open Question 1 explicitly requires that validation before this ships to real users; this document is the strong, cited starting point that validation step works from, not a substitute for it.

primarySources.name: Paul Wade — Convict Conditioning ("Big Six" 10-step bodyweight progressions: push-ups, squats, pull-ups, leg raises, bridges, handstand push-ups)
primarySources.note: A single opinionated system (as research/product-research.md flags), used here for its well-documented step names/ordering, not as an independently peer-reviewed standard.

primarySources.name: GMB Fitness — Handstand and L-Sit progression guides
Calisthenics Association — Handstand Training: Complete Progression Guide
Multiple independently-published pistol-squat progression guides (EvolveYou, PowerliftingTechnique, LiftStrong, Calisthenics Association)
primarySources.note: Cited jointly because the box/assisted/counterbalance/elevated pistol sequence is convergent across sources rather than owned by one author.

primarySources.name: Multiple independently-published muscle-up progression guides (CrossFit, WODprep, BULLBAR)
primarySources.note: Strict pull-up/dip rep thresholds before muscle-up attempts are convergent (roughly 10 strict pull-ups + 8-10 strict dips) across sources.

primarySources.name: Pilatesology — Classical Mat Exercises: Basic, Intermediate, Advanced (Joseph Pilates' original 34, as taught by his direct-lineage instructors)

confidenceLegend.high: Rep/hold threshold or ordering is convergent across 3+ independently authored sources.
confidenceLegend.medium: Sourced to a single well-documented named system (most often Convict Conditioning) or the classical Pilates curriculum; a real, citable ordering, but not independently cross-validated across multiple authors.
confidenceLegend.estimate: No single source gave an exact number; a reasoned estimate is used and flagged as such, not presented as a sourced fact.

lines.name: Push-Up Line
lines.sourceSystem: Convict Conditioning push-up progression (10 steps) + general convergent volume standard for progressing steps

threshold.note: 3x12 clean full-range reps as the widely-cited bar for branching into harder push variations.
8-10 strict full-range pull-ups is a widely convergent baseline strength benchmark across sources.

threshold.value: 10 strict pull-ups (or 5 chest-to-bar) AND 8-10 strict dips with full depth
threshold.note: Convergent across CrossFit, WODprep, and BULLBAR coaching guides as the pulling/pressing-strength gate before attempting the transition; the false-grip transition itself is a separate skill practiced once the strength gate is met.

lines.sourceSystem: Convergent strict-dip benchmark cited across muscle-up coaching guides

nodes.name: Full Strict Bar/Ring Dip (shoulders below elbows)

threshold.note: 8-10 strict full-depth dips is the convergent muscle-up-readiness benchmark.

lines.name: Squat / Single-Leg Line
lines.sourceSystem: Convict Conditioning squat progression (steps 1-7) continuing into the convergent modern pistol-squat progression (steps 8-10)

threshold.note: Box-height regression to a full pistol is convergent across EvolveYou, PowerliftingTechnique, LiftStrong, and Calisthenics Association.
First full unassisted pistol typically reached in 8-16 weeks of dedicated training per multiple independently published progressions.

lines.name: Core / Leg-Raise Line
lines.sourceSystem: Convict Conditioning leg-raise progression (10 steps), with an L-sit branch sourced from GMB Fitness and multiple independently-published L-sit guides

threshold.note: Convergent 10-15s starting hold building to a clean 30s tuck hold (no shoulder shrug / elbow bend) as the gate to one-leg extension, per GMB and multiple independent L-sit guides.

lines.name: Handstand / Skill Line
lines.sourceSystem: GMB Fitness and Calisthenics Association handstand progression guides (convergent across multiple independently-published sources)

threshold.note: Convergent 30-60s wall-hold range before attempting freestanding balance work; 45s used as the midpoint gate.
This is docs/idea.md's own illustrative example node.
The specific 30s freestanding-hold gate cited by the Calisthenics Association guide before recommending handstand push-up work.

threshold.value: 30s freestanding handstand hold AND 20 push-ups AND 10 pull-ups AND 15s L-sit
threshold.note: Full compound gate as documented by the Calisthenics Association's handstand push-up progression guide — directly validates (with real sourcing) the exact illustrative example docs/idea.md flagged as unvalidated.

tracks.name: Pilates (Classical Mat)
tracks.sourceSystem: Joseph Pilates' original 34 mat exercises (Return to Life Through Contrology), as classified into Basic/Intermediate/Advanced tiers by Pilatesology's direct-lineage classical teacher training materials
tracks.gatingModel: Classical Pilates is conventionally taught as three ORDERED TIERS (Basic -> Intermediate -> Advanced) rather than an exercise-by-exercise prerequisite tree like calisthenics — this reflects how the source material actually teaches it, not a simplification invented for this app. Exact positions 5-34 of the master sequence were not independently confirmed at high resolution in this research pass (only the opening sequence — Hundred, Roll-Up, Single Leg Circle, Rolling Like a Ball — was directly corroborated); the tier-level groupings below are drawn from Pilatesology's published Basic/Intermediate/Advanced classification, which is a real, citable secondary source, not an invented ordering.

unlockThreshold.value: All Basic-tier exercises performed with correct breath/neutral-spine form for the stated hold/rep count, confirmed via session logging.

threshold.note: Confirmed as exercise #1 of the classical sequence across all sourced references.
Confirmed as exercise #2, directly following The Hundred.
Confirmed as immediately following Single Leg Circle in the classical order.

unlockThreshold.value: All Basic-tier exercises cleanly demonstrated; Intermediate exercises layer on top rather than gating one another individually.

threshold.note: Documented as the closing exercise of the classical 34, per Pilates Bridge's 'From The Hundred To Push Up in 34 Connected Moves'.
